subject: Post-call: CuraHealth dedicated capacity needs, isolation & POC acceptance
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: CuraHealth dedicated capacity needs, isolation & POC acceptance

Samir / team — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written summary while the key asks are fresh. Please flag anything I missed.

Main pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during clinical peak windows (09:00–11:00 and 18:00–20:00 PT) causing API timeouts and degraded UX.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI isolated and auditable (SOC 2 + internal retention policy).
- Costs from bursty inference workloads; need predictable unit economics.

High-level goals
- Move to a dedicated/reserved GPU pool to meet p99 latency SLAs and isolation requirements.
- Validate a POC that demonstrates 1) tenant isolation, 2) p99 latency under target load, and 3) operational handoff/runbook.

Approx sizing and constraints (from call)
- Model: 70B family LLM (quantized).
- Baseline throughput: ~40 req/s (avg).
- Peak concurrency: ~120 req/s sustained across 30-min windows during peaks.
- Token estimate: ~250M tokens/month (inference tokens).
- Desired SLA target: p99 latency < 500ms for standard prompts during peak windows; p50 < 150ms.
- Isolation: single-tenant dedicated pool with VPC peering and encrypted KV cache.
- Ops: 24x7 on-call for sev1 during pilot window; DR/RTO expectations to be defined in SOW.

Attachments I’ve dropped with this note (stubs)
- MVP_SOW_CuraHealth.pdf — draft scope and milestone-based payment.
- SizingWorkbook_CuraHealth.xlsx — workbook with estimated GPUs and burst slots.
- SOC2-extract-2026.zip — redacted controls and evidence pointers (not the full audit).

Proposed POC acceptance criteria (short):
1) Sustained synthetic workload that reproduces your peak burst (120 req/s) for three consecutive 30-min windows without p99 > 500ms.
2) Tenant isolation verification: separate KV caches, network isolation validated via test harness.
3) End-to-end observability: token-level cost, p99/p50 dashboards, and alerting (traces and logs ingested to your Splunk/GCP).
4) Ops handoff: runbook + incident playbook delivered; runbook exercise demonstrating failover to fallback model.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- You: confirm procurement contact (Elena copied?) and sign off on the SOW draft if the scope looks right.
- We: provide detailed cost bands for steady vs. burst usage and a 30-day POC timeline.
- Technical kickoff: schedule an ops+security deep-dive this week to validate SOC2 artefacts and network design.

I’ll follow up with a formal mutual-action plan link and calendar invites. Thanks —

— Avery

Samir — thanks for the quick response. A few technical clarifications and a proposed SLA banding we can include in the SOW/POC: 

SLA banding (proposed for SOW)
- Platinum: p99 < 350ms, guaranteed throughput 150 req/s sustained, priority support & 15-min sev1 response.
- Gold: p99 < 500ms, guaranteed throughput 120 req/s, 60-min sev1 response.
- Silver: p99 < 800ms, burst-capacity best-effort, 4-hr sev1 response.

Isolation options we support (tradeoffs)
- Full single-tenant pool (recommended): physical (logical) isolation, dedicated KV cache, separate network path — best for PHI.
- Shared pool with strict namespace isolation: lower cost, slightly higher noisy-neighbor risk (mitigations: bounded per-tenant CPU/GPU slices + eviction policies).

POC acceptance checks (detailed)
1) Load validation: we will run your synthetic workload and verify p99 for three observed 30-min peak windows.
2) Audit check: we will provide an access-controlled audit log stream and a signed runbook demonstrating isolation enforcement.
3) Failure injection: single-node failure during a peak window to prove graceful degradation and fallback to a smaller model without data leakage.
4) Cost report: a 30-day token-by-token cost summary and suggested quantization/packing changes for 30% unit-cost reduction targets.

Operational support
- We will provide a dedicated onboarding engineer for week 1 (two full days of hands-on setup + one day for runbook walkthrough).
- Weekly cadence during POC: 30-min health check + one deep ops call at week midpoint.

I’ve attached a draft ops runbook (ops-runbook-draft.md) with checkpoints we’ll use during the POC. Happy to turn any of the SLA numbers up/down depending on cost tolerance — tell me which band you prefer and we’ll push that into the SOW.

— Rishi
